# Jira

Jira runs through the `jira` MCP server. Never write raw `curl` against the Jira API.

## Rules that always apply

1. **Every write is drafted first.** Show the exact comment text, worklog or field change
   and wait for a yes. Reads never need approval.
2. **Read before you write.** List existing comments or worklogs so you edit an entry
   rather than adding a near-duplicate.
3. **Never guess a status name.** Fetch the transitions and post the transition id.
4. **Never invent progress.** Describe only what the diff, the journal or the user
   actually says happened. If you cannot substantiate it, leave it out.
5. **Record what you wrote** in `docs/jira/<KEY>.md`, including the id the API returned.

## Where to look

| You need to | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Fetch an issue, search, list comments or worklogs | [references/reading.md](references/reading.md) |
| Post or edit a comment, log time, transition, edit fields | [references/writing.md](references/writing.md) |
| Follow a task end to end | [references/workflows.md](references/workflows.md) |
| Write the per-ticket journal | [references/journal.md](references/journal.md) |
| Know this project's keys, branches and statuses | [references/conventions.md](references/conventions.md) |

## The one gotcha to remember

When a request body carries text you wrote, use `/rest/api/2/`. Otherwise use `/rest/api/3/`. Version 3 demands Atlassian Document Format, a deep JSON tree. Version 2 takes a plain string. Full explanation in
[references/writing.md](references/writing.md).

## Resolving the issue key

If the user names a key, use it. Otherwise read the git branch:
`fix/ar-664-accept-invite` means `AR-664`. Two repos carry branches, `areasim-backend`
and `areasim-webapp`. If they disagree, ask which one.
